title: Form event handlers: the four attributes, their four sender types, and replacing a lookup
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a form over a custom table and a separate handler class that extends it from OUTSIDE. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="form-event-handlers"). The handler class must carry, each with the sender type the compiler requires: (1) [FormEventHandler(formStr(...), FormEventType::Initialized)] with `(xFormRun _sender, FormEventArgs _e)` - note xFormRun, NOT FormRun; (2) [FormDataSourceEventHandler(formDataSourceStr(...), FormDataSourceEventType::ValidatingWrite)] with `(FormDataSource _sender, FormDataSourceEventArgs _e)`, rejecting an invalid row through the event args; (3) [FormDataFieldEventHandler(formDataFieldStr(...), FormDataFieldEventType::Modified)] with `(FormDataObject _sender, FormDataFieldEventArgs _e)` that derives a second field from the modified one; (4) [FormControlEventHandler(formControlStr(...), FormControlEventType::Lookup)] with `(FormControl _sender, FormControlEventArgs _e)` that builds a SysTableLookup and calls _e.CancelSuperCall() - without that call BOTH the standard and the custom lookup run. A handler whose parameter profile does not match is a compile error, not a runtime surprise. Confirm every control and data source name with get_object_info on the form before writing the intrinsics. Everything must build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
